Filed: **[BUG] #6213 — https://github.com/character-ai/larch/issues/6213**. Root cause found, and it explains everything you saw, including why it hits both `/implement` and `/design`.

**The killer.** Every `larch-run.sh` `.py` invocation fires `implement kill-active-leg` on exit (trap in the template at `python/larch/state/bootstrap.py:168`). That verb reads the pgid persisted in `$IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR/.active-leg-pgid`, then blindly `killpg`s it: SIGTERM, wait 2s, SIGKILL (`python/larch/implement/dispatch_leg.py:142-157` and `:103-128`). There is no check that the pgid still names the leg that recorded it — no command-line, start-time, or parentage validation — and the kill is fully silenced (`2>/dev/null || true`, no logging).

**Why it crosses sessions.** The file is only cleared in a `finally`, so a hard-killed dispatcher (user stop, crash — or this same bug's own TERM→KILL hitting a dispatcher mid-leg, which makes it self-propagating) leaves a stale pgid behind. Your machine burns ~55k PIDs/hour with 9–10 clones running (I watched the counter wrap within the hour: session files at 42k–97k at 16:48, live processes at 6k–27k by 16:53). So a stale pgid soon points at a recycled, live, unrelated process — and long-lived Claude Code background tasks (ship drivers, `plan-review run --new-process-group` loops) are each their own process group, making them the most likely visible victims. That's your larch6 ship driver (`Terminated: 15` mid-CI-poll) and larch8's Step 3 review loop: the killer lives in implement-side cleanup, but the victim is whatever process group the recycled pid lands on, in any clone, running any skill.

**Why only this week.** The fence and pgid file landed 2026-06-25 (#5283/PR #5390) and were extended 2026-06-28 (#5769/PR #5808) — 5–8 days old — and the incident probability scales with your clone count and PID churn. Matches your onset exactly. The issue also covers a same-session variant (the file has no ownership token, so any concurrent quick py-command exiting mid-leg kills the live leg) and a smaller same-class defect in `design-step3-review.sh` (`kill -- -$_loop_pid` after the child was already reaped). I checked the old ps-scan reaper in `finalize.py` too — it's tmpdir-substring-scoped and is *not* the cross-session killer.

The issue proposes five numbered fixes: identity validation before any signal, an ownership token, the design-side reap guard, mandatory kill logging (so any future incident is attributable — today nothing records these kills anywhere, including committed run logs), and an audit of remaining persisted-PID signal sites. Dedup ran clean (nearest neighbors #5898/#5891/#4378 are related vocabulary, different defects). Until the fix lands: an unexplained "Background command … was stopped" in any clone is almost certainly this — resume the driver (both of yours resumed cleanly) rather than re-investigating; I saved a memory note to that effect. Given the severity, I'd suggest `/design 6213` next — its fix surface (`dispatch_leg.py`, `bootstrap.py`, `design-step3-review.sh`) doesn't overlap any in-flight DESIGNING/IMPLEMENTING issue I can see.
